customer_question: Adding our new Profile (X2Core) definition on top of our existing Controller Subsystem and Host Subsystem registrations is producing Core-layer Invalids. Is there a waiver we can apply for, and what should we expect for timeline if we do?
question_variants: Is there a TCW that covers Core invalids from adding a new Profile definition?
Does TCW ES-26007 apply to our situation if we haven't changed our existing Controller/Host Subsystem QDIDs?
How much extra time does filing a TCW application add to the registration?
actual_issue: Including existing, unmodified Controller Subsystem and Host Subsystem registrations and adding a new Profile (X2Core) definition produced Core-layer Invalids, and it needed to be determined whether an existing SIG waiver mechanism covered this specific situation and what procedural impact applying for it would have.
plain_english_explanation: Sometimes adding a new piece to an otherwise-unchanged Bluetooth registration trips an automated consistency check, even though nothing about the parts that were already approved actually changed. Bluetooth SIG has a specific, pre-defined exception for exactly this situation -- adding only a new profile definition without touching the existing controller and host pieces -- so instead of treating the resulting error as a dead end, the registrant can cite that specific waiver code. Using it does mean the registration has to go through an extra review step by SIG staff before it's finalized, which takes a few extra business days.
consultant_answer: Bluetooth SIG's Help & Support page, under 'ICS Form Inconsistencies for Inter-Layer Dependencies,' lists several Test Case Waiver (TCW) codes for specific Consistency Check exception scenarios. TCW ES-26007 specifically covers 'X2Core only modification/addition to waive Core invalids where no changes were made to referenced QDIDs/DNs of Core Host Configuration plus Core Controller Configuration' -- in other words, it is the exact code for Including an existing Controller Subsystem registration and an existing Host Subsystem registration, then adding a new X2Core (Profile) definition, when the resulting Core-layer Invalid is to be waived. Filing this TCW application, together with the required profile test report(s), proceeds as part of the agency registration. Because a TCW application requires SIG administrator review of the content before the registration is finalized (or a Reject notice issued to the Listing Owner if not accepted), this adds an expected 2-5 business days of registration delay compared to a registration with no TCW application.
decision_logic: Before treating a Core-layer Invalid produced by adding a new Profile (X2Core) definition to otherwise-unmodified Controller Subsystem and Host Subsystem registrations as a blocking problem, check Bluetooth SIG's published TCW list for a code matching this exact scenario (such as ES-26007) rather than assuming a waiver doesn't exist or pursuing unnecessary rework; factor the resulting SIG administrator review delay (2-5 business days) into the registration timeline once a TCW application is filed.
final_recommendation: When adding a new Profile (X2Core) definition to existing, unmodified Controller Subsystem and Host Subsystem registrations produces a Core-layer Invalid, check for and apply the matching TCW code (such as ES-26007) rather than treating the Invalid as unresolvable, and set the customer's expectations for a 2-5 business day registration delay due to the required SIG administrator review.
risk_if_done_wrong: Assuming the Core-layer Invalid from adding a new Profile definition is unresolvable, without checking for an applicable TCW, could lead to abandoning a viable registration approach or pursuing unnecessary testing. Not communicating the TCW-driven review delay could create unrealistic registration-completion expectations for the customer.
